Latin word

dēsinō

dēsinō, dēsinere, dēsiī, dēsitum

verb, third conjugation

end, come to an end; stop or cease

In this lexicon

  • end

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 24.26: aestās in autumnum dēsinit; Sall. J. 83.2: omne bellum sūmī facile, cēterum aegerrumē dēsinere (Lewis & Short)

  • stop

    the recommended word · classical

Examples

  • diem nox premit, diēs noctem, aestās in autumnum dēsinit, autumnō hiemps īnstat, quae vēre compescitur; omnia sīc trānseunt ut revertantur

    night presses on day and day on night; summer ends in autumn, winter follows hard on autumn and is checked by spring; everything passes only to come backSen. Ep. 24.26

    In the entry for end

  • nihil est aut certē exiguum est; dūrēmus; jam dēsinet

    It’s nothing, or very little anyway; let’s hold on; it will soon be overSen. Ep. 78.13

    In the entry for end

  • tum mihi nōn dubiīs auctōribus incipit aestās, et tepidī fīnem tempora vēris habent

    then, on good authority, summer begins for me, and the season of warm spring comes to an endOv. F. 5.601–602
